answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 288 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is entered against the cipher challenge, the beacon audit can replay the garden history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A farm of 529 identities would post 3642 proofs and burn roughly 42 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
